sanskrit: anuraktā mahātmānaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparakramam anujagmuḥ prayāntaṃ taṃ vanavāsāya mānavāḥ
english: The people, deeply devoted to that great-souled Rāma of true valour, followed him as he set out for his forest sojourn.

sanskrit: nivartite 'pi ca balāt suhṛdvarge ca rājini naiva te saṃnyavartanta rāmasyānugatā ratham
english: Even when the king and the circle of his friends were forcibly turned back, those who had followed Rāma's chariot would not themselves return.

sanskrit: ayodhyānilayānāṃ hi puruṣāṇāṃ mahāyaśāḥ babhūva guṇasaṃpannaḥ pūrṇacandra iva priyaḥ
english: For to the men dwelling in Ayodhyā, that one of great fame, endowed with every virtue, was as dear as the full moon.

sanskrit: sa yācyamānaḥ kākutsthaḥ svābhiḥ prakṛtibhis tadā kurvāṇaḥ pitaraṃ satyaṃ vanam evānvapadyata
english: That descendant of Kakutstha, though entreated by his own subjects, held true his word to his father and went on into the forest.

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇaḥ sasnehaṃ cakṣuṣā prapibann iva uvāca rāmaḥ snehena tāḥ prajāḥ svāḥ prajā iva
english: Gazing upon them with affection, drinking them in as it were with his eyes, Rāma addressed those subjects with the tenderness one shows one's own children.

sanskrit: yā prītir bahumānaś ca mayy ayodhyānivāsinām matpriyārthaṃ viśeṣeṇa bharate sā niveśyatām
english: "The love and high regard that you, the residents of Ayodhyā, bear toward me — let that be especially directed to Bharata for my sake.

sanskrit: sa hi kalyāṇa cāritraḥ kaikeyyānandavardhanaḥ kariṣyati yathāvad vaḥ priyāṇi ca hitāni ca
english: He is of auspicious conduct, the increaser of Kaikeyī's joy, and he will duly accomplish all that is pleasing and beneficial to you.

sanskrit: jñānavṛddho vayobālo mṛdur vīryaguṇānvitaḥ anurūpaḥ sa vo bhartā bhaviṣyati bhayāpahaḥ
english: Though young in years, he is mature in wisdom, gentle in nature, endowed with the virtue of valour — he will be a worthy lord for you and a remover of all fear.

sanskrit: sa hi rājaguṇair yukto yuvarājaḥ samīkṣitaḥ api cāpi mayā śiṣṭaiḥ kāryaṃ vo bhartṛśāsanam
english: He has been recognized as a crown prince furnished with every royal virtue. And moreover, it is your duty, as men of good conduct, to follow the command of your lord.

sanskrit: na ca tapyed yathā cāsau vanavāsaṃ gate mayi mahārājas tathā kāryo mama priyacikīrṣayā
english: And the great king must not grieve when I have gone into the forest — see to it so, I pray you, out of your desire to please me."

sanskrit: yathā yathā dāśarathir dharmam evāsthito 'bhavat tathā tathā prakṛtayo rāmaṃ patim akāmayan
english: The more that son of Daśaratha stood firm in righteousness, the more his subjects desired him as their lord.

sanskrit: bāṣpeṇa pihitaṃ dīnaṃ rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha cakarṣeva guṇair baddhvā janaṃ punar ivāsanam
english: Rāma, together with Saumitrī, seemed to draw back that wretched, tear-veiled populace by the bonds of his virtues, as if drawing them again to their seats.

sanskrit: te dvijās trividhaṃ vṛddhā jñānena vayasaujasā vayaḥprakampaśiraso dūrād ūcur idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Those brāhmaṇas, aged in the threefold manner — by knowledge, by years, and by vigour — their heads trembling with age, called out from a distance these words:

sanskrit: vahanto javanā rāmaṃ bho bho jātyās turaṃgamāḥ nivartadhvaṃ na gantavyaṃ hitā bhavata bhartari upavāhyas tu vo bhartā nāpavāhyaḥ purād vanam
english: "Ho, ho, O swift horses of noble breed that carry Rāma — turn back, you must not go on! Be loyal to your lord: your lord is one to be borne forward, not to be borne away from the city to the forest!"

sanskrit: evam ārtapralāpāṃs tān vṛddhān pralapato dvijān avekṣya sahasā rāmo rathād avatatāra ha
english: Beholding those aged brāhmaṇas lamenting in such anguished cries, Rāma suddenly descended from the chariot.

sanskrit: padbhyām eva jagāmātha sasītaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ saṃnikṛṣṭapadanyāso rāmo vanaparāyaṇaḥ
english: He then went on foot, together with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma placing his steps close to the ground, his course set upon the forest.

sanskrit: dvijātīṃs tu padātīṃs tān rāmaś cāritravatsalaḥ na śaśāka ghṛṇācakṣuḥ parimoktuṃ rathena saḥ
english: That Rāma, devoted to righteous conduct, compassionate of eye, could not bear to pass those brāhmaṇas who went on foot by riding ahead in his chariot.

sanskrit: gacchantam eva taṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ saṃbhrāntamānasāḥ ūcuḥ paramasaṃtaptā rāmaṃ vākyam idaṃ dvijāḥ
english: Seeing him walking on nonetheless, their minds overwhelmed with distress, those brāhmaṇas, utterly anguished, addressed this speech to Rāma:

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyaṃ kṛtsnam etat tvāṃ brahmaṇyam anugacchati dvijaskandhādhirūḍhās tvām agnayo 'py anuyānty amī
english: "All this entire brāhmaṇa community, devoted to brāhmaṇical conduct, follows you; even these sacred fires, borne upon the shoulders of brāhmaṇas, follow you.

sanskrit: vājapeyasamutthāni chatrāṇy etāni paśya naḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nuprayātāni haṃsān iva jalātyaye
english: Behold these parasols, earned through the Vājapeya sacrifice, following behind us like a flock of geese at the season of floods.

sanskrit: anavāptātapatrasya raśmisaṃtāpitasya te ebhiś chāyāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ svaiś chatrair vājapeyikaiḥ
english: For you who have no parasol of your own and are scorched by the sun's rays, we shall make shade with these our Vājapeya-won parasols.

sanskrit: yā hi naḥ satataṃ buddhir vedamantrānusāriṇī tvatkṛte sā kṛtā vatsa vanavāsānusāriṇī
english: The mind of ours that was ever devoted to following the Vedic hymns — for your sake, dear child, that mind has now made itself devoted to following you into the forest.

sanskrit: hṛdayeṣv avatiṣṭhante vedā ye naḥ paraṃ dhanam vatsyanty api gṛheṣv eva dārāś cāritrarakṣitāḥ
english: The Vedas, which are our highest wealth, abide within our hearts; and our wives, guarded by their own virtue, will remain in our houses.

sanskrit: na punar niścayaḥ kāryas tvadgatau sukṛtā matiḥ tvayi dharmavyapekṣe tu kiṃ syād dharmam avekṣitum
english: We shall make no further calculation about your going — our minds are nobly resolved. And when you yourself disregard dharma, what value is there in attending to dharma?

sanskrit: yācito no nivartasva haṃsaśuklaśiroruhaiḥ śirobhir nibhṛtācāra mahīpatanapāṃśulaiḥ
english: O man of self-restrained conduct, we implore you — turn back — by these our heads with hair white as swans, bowed down and grey with the dust of prostrations upon the earth.

sanskrit: bahūnāṃ vitatā yajñā dvijānāṃ ya ihāgatāḥ teṣāṃ samāptir āyattā tava vatsa nivartane
english: The many sacrifices of the brāhmaṇas who have come here are spread out and begun; their completion, dear child, depends upon your return.

sanskrit: bhaktimanti hi bhūtāni jaṃgamājaṃgamāni ca yācamāneṣu teṣu tvaṃ bhaktiṃ bhakteṣu darśaya
english: All creatures, both moving and unmoving, are filled with devotion to you. When these devotees implore you, show your devotion to your devotees.

sanskrit: anugaṃtum aśaktās tvāṃ mūlair uddhṛtavegibhiḥ unnatā vāyuvegena vikrośantīva pādapāḥ
english: These trees, unable to follow you, raised high by the force of their roots, are crying out as it were, driven by the rush of the wind.

sanskrit: niśceṣṭāhārasaṃcārā vṛkṣaikasthānaviṣṭhitāḥ pakṣiṇo 'pi prayācante sarvabhūtānukampinam
english: Even the birds, motionless, having ceased eating and moving, fixed each upon a single tree, are beseeching you, O compassionate one to all beings."

sanskrit: evaṃ vikrośatāṃ teṣāṃ dvijātīnāṃ nivartane dadṛśe tamasā tatra vārayantīva rāghavam
english: As those brāhmaṇas cried out thus imploring him to return, the river Tamasā appeared there as if blocking the way of Rāghava.

sanskrit: tatas tu tamasā tīraṃ ramyam āśritya rāghavaḥ sītām udvīkṣya saumitrim idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Rāghava, having reached the beautiful bank of the Tamasā, looked up at Sītā and spoke these words to Saumitrī:

sanskrit: iyam adya niśā pūrvā saumitre prasthitā vanam vanavāsasya bhadraṃ te sa notkaṇṭhitum arhasi
english: "This is the first night, O Saumitrī, since we set out for the forest. Good fortune in this forest sojourn — you must not be sorrowful.

sanskrit: paśya śūnyāny araṇyāni rudantīva samantataḥ yathānilayam āyadbhir nilīnāni mṛgadvijaiḥ
english: See how the forests seem to weep on every side, as the deer and birds draw near to their respective shelters and settle there.

sanskrit: adyāyodhyā tu nagarī rājadhānī pitur mama sastrīpuṃsā gatān asmāñ śociṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Today the city of Ayodhyā, my father's royal capital, will grieve for our departure, men and women alike — of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: bharataḥ khalu dharmātmā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca me dharmārthakāmasahitair vākyair āśvāsayiṣyati
english: Bharata, who is truly righteous of soul, will comfort my father and my mother with words encompassing dharma, artha, and kāma.

sanskrit: bharatasyānṛśaṃsatvaṃ saṃcintyāhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ nānuśocāmi pitaraṃ mātaraṃ cāpi lakṣmaṇa
english: Reflecting again and again upon Bharata's compassionate nature, I do not grieve for either my father or my mother, O Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tvayā kāryaṃ naravyāghra mām anuvrajatā kṛtam anveṣṭavyā hi vaidehyā rakṣaṇārthe sahāyatā
english: You, O tiger among men, have done what had to be done by following me; for the sake of protecting Vaidehī, help must be sought.

sanskrit: adbhir eva tu saumitre vatsyāmy adya niśām imām etad dhi rocate mahyaṃ vanye 'pi vividhe sati
english: But I shall pass this night, O Saumitrī, on water alone — this pleases me, even though a variety of forest food is available.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu saumitraṃ sumantram api rāghavaḥ apramattas tvam aśveṣu bhava saumyety uvāca ha
english: Having spoken thus to Saumitrī, Rāghava also addressed Sumantra: "Be vigilant, O gentle one, in attending to the horses," he said.

sanskrit: so 'śvān sumantraḥ saṃyamya sūrye 'staṃ samupāgate prabhūtayavasān kṛtvā babhūva pratyanantaraḥ
english: Sumantra, having attended to the horses, and when the sun had set, having given them abundant fodder, stood close by in readiness.

sanskrit: upāsyatu śivāṃ saṃdhyāṃ dṛṣṭvā rātrim upasthitām rāmasya śayanaṃ cakre sūtaḥ saumitriṇā saha
english: After the auspicious twilight had been duly observed and night had come, the charioteer, together with Saumitrī, prepared Rāma's bed.

sanskrit: tāṃ śayyāṃ tamasātīre vīkṣya vṛkṣadalaiḥ kṛtām rāmaḥ saumitriṇāṃ sārdhaṃ sabhāryaḥ saṃviveśa ha
english: Seeing that bed made of tree-leaves on the bank of the Tamasā, Rāma lay down upon it together with his wife and with Saumitrī.

sanskrit: sabhāryaṃ saṃprasuptaṃ taṃ bhrātaraṃ vīkṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ kathayām āsa sūtāya rāmasya vividhān guṇān
english: Seeing his brother thus fallen fast asleep with his wife, Lakṣmaṇa recounted to the charioteer the manifold virtues of Rāma.

sanskrit: jāgrato hy eva tāṃ rātriṃ saumitrer udito raviḥ sūtasya tamasātīre rāmasya bruvato guṇān
english: For Saumitrī, keeping vigil through that entire night and recounting the virtues of Rāma to the charioteer on the bank of the Tamasā, the sun rose.

sanskrit: gokulākulatīrāyās tamasāyā vidūrataḥ avasat tatra tāṃ rātriṃ rāmaḥ prakṛtibhiḥ saha
english: At a distance from the Tamasā whose banks were crowded with herds of cattle, Rāma passed that night there together with his people.

sanskrit: utthāya tu mahātejāḥ prakṛtīs tā niśāmya ca abravīd bhrātaraṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇaṃ puṇyalakṣaṇam
english: Rising up, that one of great splendour, having observed those subjects, spoke to his brother Lakṣmaṇa, he of auspicious marks:

sanskrit: asmadvyapekṣān saumitre nirapekṣān gṛheṣv api vṛkṣamūleṣu saṃsuptān paśya lakṣmaṇa sāmpratam
english: "See, O Saumitrī, these people who have abandoned all concern for us and even for their own homes are now fast asleep at the roots of the trees, O Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: yathaite niyamaṃ paurāḥ kurvanty asmannivartane api prāṇān asiṣyanti na tu tyakṣyanti niścayam
english: The manner in which these citizens are making a vow to prevent our return — they will forfeit their very lives rather than abandon their resolve.

sanskrit: yāvad eva tu saṃsuptās tāvad eva vayaṃ laghu ratham āruhya gacchāmaḥ panthānam akutobhayam
english: While they are yet asleep, let us swiftly mount the chariot and depart upon the road where no fear comes from any quarter.

sanskrit: ato bhūyo 'pi nedānīm ikṣvākupuravāsinaḥ svapeyur anuraktā māṃ vṛkṣamūlāni saṃśritāḥ
english: Hereafter again let these devoted residents of the Ikṣvāku city not sleep at the roots of trees on my account.

sanskrit: paurā hy ātmakṛtād duḥkhād vipramocyā nṛpātmajaiḥ na tu khalv ātmanā yojyā duḥkhena puravāsinaḥ
english: For it is the duty of princes to free their citizens from self-incurred suffering; certainly the people of the city must not be made to suffer through one's own actions."

sanskrit: abravīl lakṣmaṇo rāmaṃ sākṣād dharmam iva sthitam rocate me mahāprājña kṣipram āruhyatām iti
english: Lakṣmaṇa replied to Rāma, who stood there like righteousness personified: "This pleases me, O greatly wise one — let us mount at once."

sanskrit: sūtas tataḥ saṃtvaritaḥ syandanaṃ tair hayottamaiḥ yojayitvātha rāmāya prāñjaliḥ pratyavedayat
english: The charioteer then quickly harnessed the chariot with those finest of horses and, with joined palms, reported to Rāma that it was ready.

sanskrit: mohanārthaṃ tu paurāṇāṃ sūtaṃ rāmo 'bravīd vacaḥ udaṅmukhaḥ prayāhi tvaṃ ratham āsthāya sārathe
english: For the purpose of confusing the citizens, Rāma spoke these words to the charioteer: "Mount the chariot and drive northward, O charioteer.

sanskrit: muhūrtaṃ tvaritaṃ gatvā nirgataya rathaṃ punaḥ yathā na vidyuḥ paurā māṃ tathā kuru samāhitaḥ
english: Drive swiftly for a moment, then turn the chariot about and return; do this attentively so that the citizens do not discover me."

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā tathā cakre sa sārathiḥ pratyāgamya ca rāmasya syandanaṃ pratyavedayat
english: The charioteer, having heard Rāma's command, did exactly so, and having returned, reported the chariot to Rāma.

sanskrit: taṃ syandanam adhiṣṭhāya rāghavaḥ saparicchadaḥ śīghragām ākulāvartāṃ tamasām ataran nadīm
english: Rāghava, with all his equipment, mounted that chariot and crossed the swift-flowing river Tamasā with its eddying whirlpools.

sanskrit: sa saṃtīrya mahābāhuḥ śrīmāñ śivam akaṇṭakam prāpadyata mahāmārgam abhayaṃ bhayadarśinām
english: Having crossed over, that long-armed and glorious one reached the great road — auspicious, thornless, and without fear for those who fear.

sanskrit: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ paurās te rāghavo vinā śokopahataniśceṣṭā babhūvur hatacetasaḥ
english: But when night had brightened into dawn, those citizens, without Rāghava, were stunned by grief, motionless, their minds stricken.

sanskrit: śokajāśruparidyūnā vīkṣamāṇās tatas tataḥ ālokam api rāmasya na paśyanti sma duḥkhitāḥ
english: Their faces wasted with tears born of grief, looking here and there, those wretched ones could not catch even a glimpse of Rāma.

sanskrit: tato mārgānusāreṇa gatvā kiṃ cit kṣaṇaṃ punaḥ mārganāśād viṣādena mahatā samabhiplutaḥ
english: Then, having followed the road for a little while, overwhelmed by great despondency at the loss of the trail,

sanskrit: rathasya mārganāśena nyavartanta manasvinaḥ kim idaṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmo daivenopahatā iti
english: those nobly-minded men turned back at the loss of the chariot's tracks, saying: "What is this? What shall we do, struck down as we are by fate?"

sanskrit: tato yathāgatenaiva mārgeṇa klāntacetasaḥ ayodhyām agaman sarve purīṃ vyathitasajjanām
english: Then, by the very same road by which they had come, with exhausted hearts, they all went back to Ayodhyā, the city whose good people were afflicted with grief.

sanskrit: anugamya nivṛttānāṃ rāmaṃ nagaravāsinām udgatānīva sattvāni babhūvur amanasvinām
english: For the city-dwellers who had followed Rāma and now turned back, their inner beings seemed to have departed, leaving them spiritless.

sanskrit: svaṃ svaṃ nilayam āgamya putradāraiḥ samāvṛtāḥ aśrūṇi mumucuḥ sarve bāṣpeṇa pihitānanāḥ
english: Each arriving at his own dwelling, surrounded by his children and wife, all shed tears with faces veiled by weeping.

sanskrit: na cāhṛṣyan na cāmodan vaṇijo na prasārayan na cāśobhanta paṇyāni nāpacan gṛhamedhinaḥ
english: Merchants neither rejoiced nor conducted their trade; their wares held no lustre; householders did not cook.

sanskrit: naṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā nābhyanandan vipulaṃ vā dhanāgamam putraṃ prathamajaṃ labdhvā jananī nābhyanandata
english: A man who had lost his wealth felt no grief upon seeing a great windfall of riches; a mother who had obtained her first-born son felt no joy.

sanskrit: gṛhe gṛhe rudantyaś ca bhartāraṃ gṛham āgatam vyagarhayanto duḥkhārtā vāgbhis totrair iva dvipān
english: In house after house women wept and, in their anguished grief, reproached their husbands who had come home, goading them with words as one goads elephants.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu teṣāṃ gṛhaiḥ kāryaṃ kiṃ dāraiḥ kiṃ dhanena vā putrair vā kiṃ sukhair vāpi ye na paśyanti rāghavam
english: "What use are their houses to those who do not see Rāghava? What use are wives, or wealth, or sons, or even pleasures?

sanskrit: ekaḥ satpuruṣo loke lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā yo 'nugacchati kākutsthaṃ rāmaṃ paricaran vane
english: There is but one true man in this world — Lakṣmaṇa — who together with Sītā follows Kākutstha Rāma, serving him in the forest.

sanskrit: āpagāḥ kṛtapuṇyās tāḥ padminyaś ca sarāṃsi ca yeṣu snāsyati kākutstho vigāhya salilaṃ śuci
english: Blessed are those rivers, those lotus ponds and lakes, in whose pure waters Kākutstha will immerse himself and bathe.

sanskrit: śobhayiṣyanti kākutstham aṭavyo ramyakānanāḥ āpagāś ca mahānūpāḥ sānumantaś ca parvatāḥ
english: The lovely forest glades, the great marshy rivers, and the mountains with their peaks will make Kākutstha radiant.

sanskrit: kānanaṃ vāpi śailaṃ vā yaṃ rāmo 'bhigamiṣyati priyātithim iva prāptaṃ nainaṃ śakṣyanty anarcitum
english: Whatever forest or mountain Rāma approaches, none of them will be able to receive him without honouring him, as though a beloved guest had arrived.

sanskrit: vicitrakusumāpīḍā bahumañjaridhāriṇaḥ akāle cāpi mukhyāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca darśayiṣyanty anukrośād girayo rāmam āgatam
english: The mountains, adorned with garlands of varied flowers and bearing abundant clusters of blossoms, will out of compassion display to Rāma as he comes even the finest flowers and fruits out of season.

sanskrit: vidarśayanto vividhān bhūyaś citrāṃś ca nirjharān pādapāḥ parvatāgreṣu ramayiṣyanti rāghavam
english: The trees on the mountain peaks, revealing manifold and wondrous waterfalls again and again, will delight Rāghava.

sanskrit: yatra rāmo bhayaṃ nātra nāsti tatra parābhavaḥ sa hi śūro mahābāhuḥ putro daśarathasya ca
english: Where Rāma is there is no fear; there is no defeat there — for he is a hero, long-armed, and the son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: purā bhavati no dūrād anugacchāma rāghavam pādacchāyā sukhā bhartus tādṛśasya mahātmanaḥ sa hi nātho janasyāsya sa gatiḥ sa parāyaṇam
english: "Before he has gone too far, let us follow Rāghava — the shade of the feet of such a great-souled lord is a sweet comfort; for he is this people's lord, their refuge, and their final resort."

sanskrit: vayaṃ paricariṣyāmaḥ sītāṃ yūyaṃ tu rāghavam iti paurastriyo bhartṝn duḥkhārtās tat tad abruvan
english: "We women shall attend upon Sītā; you men shall attend upon Rāghava" — thus the women of the city, consumed by grief, spoke various such words to their husbands.

sanskrit: yuṣmākaṃ rāghavo 'raṇye yogakṣemaṃ vidhāsyati sītā nārījanasyāsya yogakṣemaṃ kariṣyati
english: "Rāghava will provide your welfare and security in the forest; Sītā will provide welfare and security for the women folk."

sanskrit: ko nv anenāpratītena sotkaṇṭhitajanena ca saṃprīyetāmanojñena vāsena hṛtacetasā
english: Who could find contentment in this disagreeable, joyless habitation, with its people pining and longing, their minds stolen away?

sanskrit: kaikeyyā yadi ced rājyaṃ syād adharmyam anāthavat na hi no jīvitenārthaḥ kutaḥ putraiḥ kuto dhanaiḥ
english: If the kingdom should be under Kaikeyī's sway — unrighteous and without a true protector — then we have no use for life, let alone for sons or wealth.

sanskrit: yayā putraś ca bhartā ca tyaktāv aiśvaryakāraṇāt kaṃ sā parihared anyaṃ kaikeyī kulapāṃsanī
english: She who has abandoned both her son and her husband for the sake of power — that Kaikeyī, the disgrace of her lineage — whom else would she spare?

sanskrit: kaikeyyā na vayaṃ rājye bhṛtakā nivasemahi jīvantyā jātu jīvantyaḥ putrair api śapāmahe
english: We shall never dwell in the kingdom as hirelings of Kaikeyī — we swear this by our very lives and by the lives of our children!

sanskrit: yā putraṃ pārthivendrasya pravāsayati nirghṛṇā kas tāṃ prāpya sukhaṃ jīved adharmyāṃ duṣṭacāriṇīm
english: She who mercilessly sends the son of the king of kings into exile — that unrighteous, wickedly acting woman — who could live happily under her sway?

sanskrit: na hi pravrajite rāme jīviṣyati mahīpatiḥ mṛte daśarathe vyaktaṃ vilopas tadanantaram
english: For the lord of the earth will not survive when Rāma has gone into exile; when Daśaratha dies, clearly devastation will follow.

sanskrit: te viṣaṃ pibatāloḍya kṣīṇapuṇyāḥ sudurgatāḥ rāghavaṃ vānugacchadhvam aśrutiṃ vāpi gacchata
english: "Those of you whose merit is exhausted and who are truly wretched — drink poison mixed and prepared, or follow Rāghava, or go where you will never hear of him again."

sanskrit: mithyā pravrājito rāmaḥ sabhāryaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ bharate saṃniṣṛṣṭāḥ smaḥ saunike paśavo yathā
english: Rāma has been wrongfully sent into exile, together with his wife and Lakṣmaṇa; we have been handed over to Bharata like animals to a butcher.

sanskrit: tās tathā vilapantyas tu nagare nāgarastriyaḥ cukruśur bhṛśasaṃtaptā mṛtyor iva bhayāgame
english: The women of the city, lamenting thus, cried out in fierce anguish as though at the approach of death.

sanskrit: tathā striyo rāmanimittam āturā yathā sute bhrātari vā vivāsite vilapya dīnā rurudur vicetasaḥ sutair hi tāsām adhiko hi so 'bhavat
english: Those women, afflicted on Rāma's account, wept and lamented helplessly as though their own son or brother had been sent away — for he had become dearer to them than their own sons.
